items.expected_claim: computes phonon modes by evaluating second-derivative Hessian matrices of an E(3)-equivariant energy model trained on energy and force data — no direct phonon supervision required
Hessian serves as higher-order training signal, improving energy models beyond energy/force-only training
derives symmetry constraints for IR/Raman active modes from phonon mode irreducible representations
introduces vector, matrix, and momentum-dependent matrix virtual nodes to GNN, enabling direct prediction of Γ-phonon spectra and full dispersion from atomic coordinates only
handles material-dependent variable-length output (phonon modes) — a challenge standard invariant GNNs cannot address directly
built Γ-phonon database for over 140,000 Materials Project structures (146,323 total); validated on SiGe, FeCoNi, NiFe, and multi-component high-entropy alloy systems

fine-tunes MACE exclusively on forces (no energy loss term) using ~6 randomly all-atom-perturbed supercells per material — a compact phonon-targeted training strategy covering 77 elements from 2,738 structures

force MAE of 20.5 meV/Å on phonon-relevant perturbations vs. 71–78 meV/Å for general-purpose universal MLIPs (M3GNet, GPTFF, MLUHIP); phonon frequency MAE 0.18 THz with R² = 0.997 on 384 held-out materials
including energy in the loss (MACE-FE) degrades force MAE from 20.5 to 23.8 meV/Å — force-only fine-tuning is the preferred strategy for phonon applications even when a general MLIP underperforms

items.expected_claim: CGCNN learns material properties directly from a crystal graph without constructing a fixed-length global descriptor — universal across 87 elements, 7 lattice systems, and 216 space groups; demonstrated on 46,744 Materials Project structures

ACE provides a complete, systematically improvable descriptor of local atomic environments with O(N) linear evaluation cost irrespective of expansion order — encompasses SOAP and moment tensors as special cases

ACE formally supports arbitrary multi-component systems by coupling chemical and geometric channels in the atomic basis — enabling systematic treatment of compositional diversity without per-species re-parameterization, and is identified in the ACE paper as a natural foundation for combination with neural network function approximators

uses continuous-filter convolutional (cfconv) layers where a filter-generating network maps interatomic distances to continuous filter values — operates directly on atom types and 3D positions without pre-defined descriptors
learns atom-wise representations respecting rotational, translational, and permutational invariances by construction: distances expanded in Gaussian basis ensure rotational invariance
